subject: chemistry
title: Mass spectrometry and relative atomic mass
key_idea: Atomic masses are measured on a scale where carbon-12 is the standard. A **mass spectrometer** separates ions by their mass-to-charge ratio and shows how much of each isotope there is. The **relative atomic mass** is the weighted mean of the isotope masses.

blocks.text: Atoms are far too light to weigh in grams, so masses are compared with a standard. The standard is the carbon-12 atom.

items.meaning: One twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
The mass of an atom of an isotope compared with one twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element, compared with one twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
The weighted mean mass of a molecule, compared with one twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.
The same idea for a compound with a giant structure, such as an ionic compound, using its formula unit.

items: Relative masses are ratios, so they have **no units**.
Aᵣ is a weighted mean because an element is a mixture of isotopes, each with its own abundance.
Aᵣ is usually not a whole number, but a relative isotopic mass is very close to the mass number.

blocks.label: Relative molecular or formula mass
blocks.formula: Mᵣ = sum of the Aᵣ values of all the atoms in the formula
where: Aᵣ values are read from the Periodic Table
multiply an Aᵣ by the number of atoms of that element

items.text: Calcium chloride is CaCl₂, with one Ca and two Cl.
CaCl₂ is ionic with a giant structure, so 111.1 is its relative formula mass. For a simple molecule, such as H₂O, it is the relative molecular mass.

items: Every relative mass is compared with one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
Aᵣ is a weighted mean over the isotopes of the element.
Mᵣ is the sum of the Aᵣ values in the formula. Use relative formula mass for giant structures.

blocks.text: A mass spectrometer measures the mass of ions and how many of each there are. In a time of flight (TOF) instrument, ions are separated by how long they take to travel along a tube.

diagram.alt: A flow diagram of a time of flight mass spectrometer: ionisation, acceleration, ion drift, detection and data analysis.

items: **Ionisation:** the sample is turned into positive ions.
**Acceleration:** an electric field accelerates the ions so that they all have the same kinetic energy.
**Ion drift:** the ions pass along a flight tube. Lighter ions move faster, so they arrive first.
**Detection:** each ion that arrives gains an electron and makes a tiny current. The current shows how many ions arrived.
**Data analysis:** a computer turns the arrival times into a mass spectrum.
The horizontal axis is **m/z**, the mass-to-charge ratio, also written m/e. For ions with a 1+ charge, m/z equals the mass of the ion.
The height of each peak is the relative abundance of that ion.
The spectrum of an element has one peak for each isotope, so it identifies the element and its isotopes.
The peak at the largest m/z for a molecule is the molecular ion, M⁺. Its m/z value is the relative molecular mass.
Lighter ions travel faster along the flight tube and reach the detector first.
The m/z values give the isotope masses and the peak heights give their abundances.
The molecular ion peak, M⁺, gives the relative molecular mass.

sections.heading: Finding relative atomic mass from a spectrum

blocks.text: To find Aᵣ, multiply each isotope's mass by its abundance, add the results, and divide by the total abundance. This section covers the method, and how to work backwards.

blocks.label: Relative atomic mass
where: isotopic mass, from the m/z of each peak
abundance, as a percentage or as a peak height
Σ means add up for every isotope

items.text: A magnesium spectrum has peaks at m/z 24 (78.6%), 25 (10.1%) and 26 (11.3%).

diagram.alt: A practice question: find the relative atomic mass of chlorine from the abundance of chlorine-35 and chlorine-37.
diagram.question: A sample of chlorine contains {p}% of chlorine-35 (mass 35) and the rest chlorine-37 (mass 37). Calculate its relative atomic mass to 1 decimal place.
working: Chlorine-37 makes up the rest, which is (100 − {p})%.

blocks.text: If Aᵣ is known, the abundance can be found. Boron has isotopes of mass 10 and 11 and Aᵣ = 10.8. Let x be the % of mass 10. Then 10x + 11(100 − x) = 1080, so x = 20%.

items: Aᵣ = total of (mass × abundance) ÷ total abundance.
Use the same abundance units for every peak, then divide by their total.
An unknown abundance can be found by setting up the same equation and solving it.

checks.a: The weighted mean mass of an atom of an element compared with one twelfth of the mass of an atom of carbon-12.

checks.q: A sample of neon has peaks at m/z 20 (90.5%), 21 (0.3%) and 22 (9.2%). Calculate its relative atomic mass to 1 decimal place.
State what happens to the ions in the ion drift stage of a time of flight mass spectrometer, and why lighter ions are detected first.
checks.a: The ions travel along a flight tube. All the ions have the same kinetic energy, so lighter ions have a greater speed and reach the detector sooner.

items: Use the term **relative molecular mass** for simple molecules and **relative formula mass** for compounds with giant structures.
Mass spectrometry questions are limited to ions with a single positive charge, so m/z equals the isotopic mass.
Learn the definitions of relative isotopic mass and relative atomic mass. The definitions of relative molecular mass and relative formula mass are not required.

blocks.text: A diatomic molecule gives several molecular ion peaks, because each atom can be either isotope. This section predicts the spectrum of chlorine, Cl₂.
Chlorine is about 75% ³⁵Cl and 25% ³⁷Cl, a ratio of 3 : 1. The chance of each pair follows from this ratio.

items: The 72 peak is tall because a ³⁵Cl atom and a ³⁷Cl atom can pair up in two ways.
The peaks at 70, 72 and 74 are in the ratio 9 : 6 : 1.
Cl₂ also breaks up, giving peaks for Cl⁺ at m/z 35 and 37 in the ratio 3 : 1.
The molecular ion M⁺ is the ion with the largest m/z in the spectrum. Its m/z gives the relative molecular mass.
Cl₂ has molecular ion peaks at 70, 72 and 74 in the ratio 9 : 6 : 1.
The m/z value of M⁺ is the relative molecular mass.

blocks.text: The ionisation stage can be done in two ways. Both give positive ions.

items: **Electron impact:** the sample is vaporised and bombarded with high-energy electrons. Each atom or molecule loses an electron: X(g) → X⁺(g) + e⁻.
**Electrospray ionisation:** the sample is dissolved in a volatile solvent and forced through a fine needle at high voltage. It gains a proton: X(g) + H⁺ → XH⁺(g).
With electrospray, the m/z of the peak is one more than the mass of X, so subtract 1 to find the relative molecular mass.
At the detector, the ions gain electrons and produce a current that is proportional to the abundance of the ions.

blocks.label: Kinetic energy of an ion
where: m, the mass of the ion
v, the speed of the ion

blocks.text: All the ions are accelerated to the same kinetic energy, so a smaller m means a larger v. Time of flight is t = d ÷ v, where d is the length of the flight tube. Lighter ions have a shorter time of flight.

items: Ionisation is by electron impact or electrospray.
Equal kinetic energy means lighter ions travel faster and arrive sooner.
Define the unified atomic mass unit as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, and define each relative mass in terms of it.
Relative molecular mass and relative formula mass are both written Mᵣ.
Mass spectra are read in terms of m/e values and isotopic abundances. How the instrument works is not required.
Aᵣ can be calculated from a table of abundances or directly from a mass spectrum.
